title: EXPLAINER | The Famous Bird App Before and During Elon Musk’s Acquisition
explanation: Twitter’s acquisition by Elon Musk transformed ownership, staffing, verification, moderation, branding, and platform strategy. The change illustrates how a single private owner can rapidly reshape a communications network used by journalists, governments, activists, businesses, and citizens. Platform governance is therefore partly a question of corporate power over public conversation.
why: Social platforms function like communications infrastructure even when privately owned. Changes in moderation and verification can affect Philippine news, politics, emergency information, and harassment.

title: EXPLAINER | The Push for Divorce in the Philippines
explanation: The Philippine divorce debate concerns whether couples in failed marriages should have an accessible legal mechanism to permanently dissolve the union. Existing remedies such as annulment or declaration of nullity address different legal conditions and can be costly or complex. Divorce legislation would need rules for grounds, property, support, custody, and protection from abuse.
why: Family law affects real households, not abstract ideology. The design of any divorce system determines whether relief is practical for ordinary people or only the wealthy.

title: EXPLAINER | Same-sex Marriage vs Same-sex Civil Union: What’s the Difference?
explanation: Marriage and civil union can both provide legal recognition to couples, but the rights attached to each depend on the law. Differences may involve inheritance, adoption, tax treatment, property, medical decisions, immigration, social benefits, and symbolic status. A civil union is not automatically equivalent to marriage unless legislation gives it equivalent rights.
why: Same-sex couples can build long-term families while lacking many automatic legal protections. The distinction affects practical issues during illness, death, property disputes, and family emergencies.

title: EXPLAINER | Tracing What You Need to Know about the SIM Card Registration Act
explanation: The SIM Registration Act was introduced to connect mobile numbers with verified identities and reduce anonymous misuse such as scams and threats. Its effectiveness depends on identity verification, enforcement against fraudulent registration, cybersecurity, telecom compliance, and public awareness. It is not a complete anti-scam solution because fraud adapts to new controls.
why: Mobile phones are central to banking, commerce, communication, and emergency services. The law’s success should be measured against both crime reduction and protection of personal data.

title: EXPLAINER | When #PaengPH Went Trick or Treating in Southern Philippines
explanation: Tropical Storm Paeng demonstrated how a weather system need not be the strongest possible cyclone to cause catastrophic flooding and landslides. Rainfall, soil saturation, river systems, terrain, settlement location, and preparedness determine disaster severity. Areas outside the expected center track can still receive deadly rainfall.
why: Focusing only on storm category can create false security. Rainfall and hazard warnings are often more relevant to household safety than wind classification alone.

title: Bakit humihina ang halaga ng peso laban sa dolyar?
explanation: The peso-dollar exchange rate moves because of interest rates, inflation, trade flows, investment, remittances, global risk, central-bank policy, and demand for U.S. dollars. A weaker peso makes imports such as fuel and some food or equipment more expensive, while exporters and families receiving dollar remittances may receive more pesos. Currency weakness is therefore neither purely good nor purely bad; effects differ across sectors.
why: Exchange rates influence fuel, electricity, travel, imported goods, business costs, government debt, and OFW remittances. Understanding the mechanism helps explain why global financial decisions show up in local prices.
